title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 13
paragraphs: Having said this, the figure, as it seemed to Xerxes, flew away. When day dawned he took no account of the dream, but gathered together the same Persians he had assembled before and said to them: “Persians, forgive me for making such quick changes in my counsel, for I am not yet at my prime in judgment, and those who are advising me to do the things I spoke of do not leave me to myself for long. But when at first I heard the opinion of Artabanus, my youthful spirit burst out, and I cast unseemly words at a man older than myself; now, however, I acknowledge he is right, and I shall follow his advice. Know, then, that I have changed my mind about marching against Greece — and you may remain at rest.”
